description: The Settings dialog's Access page (Baude's, Record's and the phone's; on the phone the fifth page of Settings, switched to by the bar at its foot): for the host picked beside New session, who in the mesh may use each of its capabilities, as it answers access. The host enforces each rule on the wire ops the capability uses (baudelib/access.py, PhoneAccess.kt): a member it refuses is answered access_denied, and a head on the host's own machine, or over ssh, is never refused. Who's asking comes from the signed open of the member's tunnel (mesh.py), or, for a chat's own tools, the member that started the chat.
opens: Settings… → Access (the dialog's page switcher; the phone's: the bar at Settings' foot)

parts.name: Host
parts.shows: Row "Host" with the picked host's name after it (dim), as Telemetry's.

parts.name: Capability rows
parts.shows: One boxed list, a row for each capability in this order: Shell, Emission Browser, Providers, Model Files, Agent Spawn, Agent Management, Kubernetes, Databases, Access Rules. Each row is the capability's name and a dropdown after it: Everybody, Nobody or Chosen Members. With Chosen Members, a switch row for each member the host can name (those it reaches, has lately, or a rule names), on for those chosen; on the desktop they are the row's expanded rows, on the phone the rows under it, indented. With no other member: one dim row "No other members". Rows the asking app may not change (editable false: a member the Access Rules rule refuses) are greyed.

actions.by: pick in the dropdown, or switch a member
actions.does: Sends access_set at once (capability, rule) and shows the rule as the host answers; picking Chosen Members opens the member rows. A refusal says "Couldn't change access: <why>" in a toast and the row goes back to what the host has.

decisions.said: The owner wants to configure who may use each of a host's capabilities from the mesh: everybody, nobody, or chosen principals; shell through Multiplex, the Emission browser, providers, model files, agent spawn, managing existing agents, Kubernetes and databases (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Settings has an Access page after Telemetry: a row for each capability with Everybody / Nobody / Chosen Members, the members chosen by switches; the host keeps the rules and enforces them on the wire, never only in the UI

decisions.said: The UI for this should be in Settings (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Access rules are set in Settings → Access on every app, for the host picked beside New session

decisions.said: The Access Rules capability defaults to Nobody: only local and ssh heads change rules until members are listed (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Access Rules starts at Nobody; every other capability at Everybody

decisions.said: A rule is only as good as its weakest path; who is asking must come from the authenticated link, not a claim a member can forge (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every op reaching a capability's effect is guarded by it (reading a chat's folder, git and @ names by Agent Management, Kubernetes and databases parts of @ by theirs, host-admin ops by Access Rules, approving commands by Shell, Bots by Shell and Emission Browser), and members are told by their signed keys

parts.name: Meta's rows
parts.shows: Meta has a setting for each capability (access_<capability>), read on every host of the mesh, in its index as "<host>: <rule>; …" (everybody, nobody, or chosen: the members' names), looked up off the main loop. Meta may set a rule narrower itself ([<host>:] nobody, or chosen with fewer members); a wider one it shows for the user. Shown under a reply (show setting:access_<capability>), it is a row for each host, titled "<host> / <capability>" with its dropdown, greyed where that host's Access Rules refuse this one.

decisions.said: Meta should help configure access and show UI for the altered attributes, like a row of the host and the capability with a dropdown (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app's Meta can show a host's access rule as a "<host> / <capability>" row with its dropdown; the rule is the user's to change there

decisions.said: Meta may narrow a rule itself; widening shows the row for the user to flip; rows for any mesh host, not only this machine's (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Meta narrows access rules on any host itself and shows the row for a wider one; it never widens one

states: default: every rule Everybody but Access Rules, Nobody (a mesh with no rules works as before; only this machine's heads, and those over ssh, change the rules till members are chosen)
error: the host's error in one dim row
no members: "No other members" under Chosen Members
